quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should a motorcycle rider position themselves in the lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or from the front. Riding too close to the passing vehicle is dangerous for both of you.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: Right
Center
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When at an intersection, does eye contact with an oncoming driver mean they see you?

options.text: Yes, it is a good way to know that the driver sees you.
No, eye contact does not mean the driver sees you.
Yes, it is required before proceeding through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, eye contact does not mean the driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver sees your motorcycle. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles without actually noticing them.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.
You have space to maneuver.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely. This increases your escape options, not limits them.

questions.question: Which is NOT a common type of helmet?

options.text: One-half
Three-quarter
Full-face

questions.correctAnswerText: One-half
questions.explanation: The common helmet types are three-quarter and full-face. Full-face helmets offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while you stop on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You can usually stay in control.
You will likely lose control.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually stay in control.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks during a straight stop, you can keep it locked until you fully stop. A locked rear wheel on a straight path usually does not cause loss of control.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign appears on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slow or stopped, should a motorcyclist weave between lanes?

options.text: No, a motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
Yes, it is acceptable to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Yes, ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, a motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to operate safely.

questions.question: You are passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic. Where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid hazards like opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more safety space.

questions.question: You should keep more distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles if:

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
Traffic is light.
You can see through the vehicles in front of you to check traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Keep at least a four-second distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: A helmet will give you the most protection if it has all of these qualities, except:

options.text: It meets U.S. DOT standards.
It is loose-fitting.
It has no damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fit snugly around your head, and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: At speeds over 55 mph.
At speeds below 30 mph.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: At speeds below 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 mph and on short trips of less than five miles.

questions.question: What is the difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, a rider should:

options.text: Use their arms to steer, not to hold themselves up.
Sit far back so their arms are straight when reaching the handlebars.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use their arms to steer, not to hold themselves up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms are slightly bent and you can use them to steer. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly and maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What does a red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.
No, it is recommended but not required.
It is only required for new motorcycle riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: The law requires all motorcycle riders to wear eye protection. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.
0.3 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: It is illegal for riders age 21 and older to ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Riders under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even below the legal limit, it may be unsafe to ride.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists must pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: If passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may disregard no passing zone markings if you began the pass in a passing zone.
You must observe the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must observe the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must follow the speed limit and only pass where it is legal to do so.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if it is safe. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distances. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder of the road to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled railroad tracks in your lane. Changing your angle may cause you to enter another lane and hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down, let the dog approach, and accelerate away from the animal.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog approach, and accelerate away from the animal.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and let it come closer. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look downward to see the changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up on scored pavement. Ride slowly, maintain steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.
